topic: How do atmospheric turbulence models like HVM affect optical link budget margin calculations for varying ground station altitudes?
response: Atmospheric turbulence models like HVM affect optical link budget margin calculations by introducing uncertainty in beam pointing quality and causing signal intensity scintillation. For varying ground station altitudes, the amount of atmospheric turbulence crossed by the link is influenced by altitude, time of day, and temporary meteorological conditions. This affects the achievable data rates, which depend on link distance (free space loss) and atmospheric transmissivity.
reference_context: The reference context discusses optical ground-to-space links, including the effect of atmospheric refraction turbulence (IRT) along the first 1-2 km of the optical path close to the origin of the uplink. The Hufnagel-Valley Model (HVM) is mentioned as a modified model used for height profiles.
